summary: The appellant sought compassionate appointment as a Junior Clerk under the Orissa Civil Service (Rehabilitation Assistance) Rules, 1990, following the death of his father, a government servant, in 2010. His application was delayed for five years without action, despite fulfilling eligibility criteria including financial need and maternal medical unfitness. The 1990 Rules were replaced by the 2020 Rules, which limited compassionate appointments to 'Group D' posts. The High Court upheld consideration under the 2020 Rules. The Supreme Court examined conflicting precedents on whether the scheme at the time of death or at the time of decision applies. While acknowledging the legal conflict, the Court ruled in favor of applying the 1990 Rules due to the appellant's lack of fault and prolonged inaction by authorities.
legal_provisions_cited: Indian Bank and others v. Promila and another (2020) 2 SCC 729
State of Madhya Pradesh v. Amit Shrivas (2020) 10 SCC 496
State of Madhya Pradesh v. Ashish Awasthi (2021)
The Chief General Manager, Telecommunication, BSNL v. Vidya Prasad (2021)
The Secretary to Govt. Department of Education (Primary) and others v. Bheemesh alias Bheemappa, 2021 SCC OnLine SC 1264
N.C. Santosh v. State of Karnataka (2020) 7 SCC 617
final_judgment: The appeal was allowed; the appellant is entitled to compassionate appointment under the 1990 Rules, and the State is directed to consider his claim accordingly.
